purpose: Sodium bicarbonate is used to relieve heartburn, acid indigestion, and upset stomach. It is also used in hospitals to treat conditions where the blood becomes too acidic. Sometimes it is used to make the urine less acidic, which can help certain medications work better or help prevent kidney stones.
how_it_works: Think of it as a natural neutralizer — it works by directly canceling out excess stomach acid, kind of like baking soda neutralizing vinegar. When you take it, it reacts with the acid in your stomach and quickly reduces that burning feeling. In the bloodstream, it helps restore the normal acid-balance that your body needs to function properly.
common_side_effects: Common side effects include burping, gas, and bloating. You may also notice your stomach feeling temporarily full or uncomfortable. If taken in large amounts over time, it can cause nausea, headache, or swelling in your hands and feet.
warnings: Do not take this medication for more than 2 weeks without talking to your doctor. People on a low-sodium diet should be careful, as it contains sodium and can raise blood pressure. Avoid taking it right after a large meal, as it can cause your stomach to burst in rare cases. If you have kidney disease, heart problems, or are pregnant, check with your doctor before using it. Do not mix it with other antacids without asking your pharmacist first.
typical_dosing: For heartburn in adults, a typical dose is half a teaspoon dissolved in a glass of water, taken every 2 hours as needed, but no more than 7 doses in 24 hours. For people over 60, no more than 3 doses in 24 hours. Always follow the directions on the label or from your doctor, as dosing can vary depending on what it is being used for.
